answer: Coordination Depth Pricing. Each identity must append a fresh, verifiable whisper of work to a per-agent chain, and pairing claims are admitted only if their combined history depth clears a rising threshold tied to current cluster size. Attackers therefore pay a real marginal cost in serialized proofs for every extra identity, since parallel fabrication cannot shortcut depth. A sparse quartz timestamp seals each append, while stale shale receipts are rejected as depth evidence, so mass-produced identities fail admission.
